a.title: The answer

a.text: The answer: The table lives in ordinary memory, and one register

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: (the PTBR, called satp on RISC-V) holds the address where it

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: starts. A row is a frame number plus a few bits: valid, R, W, X

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: and U. The OS writes rows (mappages in xv6), the hardware reads

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: them, and a row without the valid bit traps; …
